requirements.requirement: Stop usb-storage kernel module from loading now (immediate effect)
requirements.summary: Baseline confirmed usb-storage was not loaded and no prior blacklist existed (cmd-02e91ddd8e394736, cmd-a135dbb450b24443, cmd-24d994c62cbf4e75). Created /etc/modprobe.d/usb-storage-blacklist.conf with 'blacklist usb-storage' and 'install usb-storage /bin/false' (cmd-2c60643548e44496). Verified immediately that modprobe usb-storage fails with 'Operation not permitted' and lsmod shows no usb_storage loaded (cmd-08f6549a62e94059).

requirements.requirement: Stop usb-storage kernel module from loading after a reboot (persistence)
requirements.summary: Initramfs was rebuilt with dracut -f to embed the blacklist in early boot (cmd-339a303ebff44ff5), and lsinitrd confirmed the config file was present in the new image (cmd-713ed4e1df524bd4). A pre-restart boot identity and healthy baseline were captured (cmd-801ae09228d248bb), the node was rebooted via 'shutdown -r now' with acknowledgement returned before disconnect (cmd-0e120c25fb6549da), the node was observed unreachable during the transition (cmd-6a03120f62d14d45, cmd-9c404e1cb727471c), and a new, different boot_id was observed after reconnect (cmd-1d6d8770a97349b5), confirming a genuine restart. Post-reboot verification directly shows the blacklist file still present, usb_storage absent from lsmod, modprobe still failing, and a fresh uptime timestamp (cmd-4d37b33bae3a40a6). This is a complete before/during-disruption/after transition, not just configuration.

overall_summary: The executor blacklisted usb-storage via /etc/modprobe.d and an install-to-/bin/false override, rebuilt the initramfs so the block applies at early boot, and directly demonstrated both immediate blocking (before reboot) and persistence across an actual reboot cycle with a verified change in boot identity and post-reboot confirmation that the module remains blocked. Both material outcomes of the task are satisfied with direct, first-hand evidence rather than configuration alone.
limitations: Package-health checks were unavailable (timed out) in both lifecycle snapshots, so native package-manager consistency could not be independently verified, though this is unrelated to the task's material outcomes.

No further reboot cycles were captured beyond the single mandatory restart, so long-term persistence across multiple future reboots is inferred from the initramfs rebuild plus one successful reboot rather than directly observed multiple times.

operational_hygiene.summary: Every state-changing command has a clear, direct link to the task: creating the blacklist config (cmd-2c60643548e44496), rebuilding initramfs (cmd-339a303ebff44ff5), and the mandatory node restart (cmd-0e120c25fb6549da). The lifecycle diff shows only expected residue: /tmp/dracut.log and /tmp/reboot.log, which are direct low-risk byproducts of the dracut rebuild and background reboot trigger, not abandoned experiments. No failed services, no unexpected listening-socket changes beyond PID renumbering from the reboot, and no destructive or unrelated mutations were found in the executor timeline.
